claims.source_quote_ar: يَجُوزُ أَنْ يكون مِنْهُم رَافعا لمن لِأَنَّهُ قد وصف بِهِ رسلًا وَأَن يَكُونَ مُبْتَدَأً وَخَبَرًا، وَالْجُمْلَةُ نَعْتٌ لِرُسُلٍ، وَأَنْ يَكُونَ مُسْتَأْنَفًا.
claims.claim_ar: يجوز عدة أوجھ لإعراب جملة «مِنْ… مَنْ …»: أن تكون رافعة (مِنْهُم رافعًا لمن)، أو أن تكون «مَنْ…» مبتدأً وتكون الجملة خبرًا، أو أن تكون الجملة نعتًا لِـرُسُلٍ، أو أن تكون جملة مستأنفة.
claims.claim_en: Several alternative analyses are permissible for the construction 'min ... man ...': it may function as a 'rafʿ' (raising) construction, or 'man...' may be the mubtada' with the following clause as its khabar, or the whole clause may be a qualifying adjective (na't) to 'rusul' (messengers), or it may be a resumed (musta'nafa) clause.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source lists multiple, alternative readings; the phrase 'رافعًا لمن' is somewhat terse and requires review to map precisely to the construction in this ayah (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ…).

claims.claim_ar: من الممكن إعراب «مَنْ...» كمبتدأ وتكون الجملة التالية خبرًا له.
claims.claim_en: It is possible to parse 'man...' as the subject (mubtada') with the following clause acting as its predicate (khabar).
claims.needs_review_reason: Applicability to this specific verse (where the construction is «مِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ…») should be checked; the source states a general permissibility.

claims.claim_ar: إحدى وجوه الإعراب أن تكون الجملة «مَنْ...» نعتًا لـ«رُسُلٍ» (أي متعلقة بوصف الرسل).
claims.claim_en: One permissible analysis is that the clause 'man...' is a genitive/adjectival clause (na't) qualifying 'rusul' (messengers).
claims.needs_review_reason: The source refers to 'رسُلًا' in its example; verify whether that governor exists or is implied in this verse's context.

warnings: The cited analysis in the source discusses the pattern «مِنْهُمْ مَنْ…» and examples with «مِنْهُمْ» or «رسُلًا». The verse at hand uses «وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ…». Confirm that the source's observations transfer unchanged to «مِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ…» in this context.
The phrase «رافعًا لمن» in the source is terse and potentially ambiguous; it should be reviewed by a specialist to determine the precise grammatical operation intended by al-ʿUkbarī.
